speechtext:
Mr. Chairman, I had not intended to deal further with this matter, but in view of the remark just made I think I should say something. The remarks of the hon. member for Kootenay East (Mr. Stevens) are much along the lines of what was in the minds of those who first desired this legislation and who had something to do with its drafting. It was felt that the present control over the marketing of live stock should be made to conform more with what is being done than was possible under the previous legislation. The methods by which live stock is marketed to-day are different from those which were used when the stockyards were originally set up. At the time the stockyards were set up there is no doubt it was the intention to direct all live stock into the stockyards so that anyone desiring to purchase would have to go there in order to obtain his live stock. But, as everyone knows, since trucks began to be used live stock has been trucked over long distances. At the beginning of his discussion the hon. member for Kootenay East mentioned 200 miles, but I may say that live stock from my own farm is. trucked close to 350 miles into Winnipeg. The truckers leave in the evening and they are in Winnipeg early the next day.
There is not a farmer but knows that in many instances he gets better service at certain times of the year from such trucking than he would get even from the railroads. The packers know they can direct these truckers to their packing plant past the stockyard. When live stock is taken past the stockyard directly to the packing plant any control which we may have over the stockyard is of no avail. The intention of this legislation is to provide greater control. Something was said with regard to the exchanges handling the stockyards, but as was said when the second reading of this bill was under consideration, there are eleven stockyards but only six have exchanges.

speechtext: Which six?

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: I have not the names in mind just at the moment.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: It would be the larger ones.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext:
Yes. In so far as a packer having an interest in a stockyard is concerned, there is a section of the bill which makes it impossible for a packer to operate a stockyard if at the same time he intends to buy live stock. That is the intention of the legislation, and if it does pot work out, we will consider it when we come to it. It is the intention that the owner of a stockyard . shall not be directly interested in the purchasing of live stock.

Then there is another point to be considered in relation to what has been said. The objective of any organization, no matter what it may be, that sees fit to own and operate a stockyard is to get all the business it possibly can get into that stockyard. It would have no other reason for operating, so why should it have any particular reason to encourage live stock to pass the stockyard and go to the packing plant to promote the interests of the packing plant. Its whole interest is to get business into the stockyard, so to operate the yard as to see that the business does go there.
The bill does provide greater control over the packers' yards to which truckers may go or to which stock may be taken by other means. The bill provides for greater control than has ever been exercised in any previous legislation. I do not think there is any particular reason for saying that this legislation is drafted for the purpose of taking away from someone who might properly operate a stockyard the control over the marketing of stock, as against any control which may be exercised by the packers themselves. The intention is the very opposite. I do not think it is necessary to appear to be defending the packers or to be saying anything in their defence. There is a great deal of criticism of the packers all across the country, some of that criticism justified and some of it probably not justified. In any event, this legislation is intended to regulate the trade in a manner which will give less control to the packer than he has under the legislation which exists at the present time. speechtext:
What is the explanation

What work

16.	Administration of Animal Contagious Diseases Act and Meat and Canned Foods Act, $1,677,981.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext:
What is the
government doing this year about the epidemic of encephalomyelitis? There are still some cases in the west.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: This work is carried on mostly by the provinces, but we are giving whatever assistance we can. They ask from time to time for the assistance of some of our officials, particularly our veterinarians, who give whatever assistance they can.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext:
Do we supply the
serum or do the - provinces?

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: The provinces.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext:
Is any compensation paid
for losses sustained?

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: No.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext:
I understand that the
vaccine is obtained from two laboratories in the Llnited States, one in New York and the other in California. Is it not possible to get that vaccine in the dominion? Cannot our laboratories prepare it?

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext:
The serum is being
made at the university of Saskatoon. I am not sure about the other laboratories. Most of the serum last year was obtained from the United States, as the hon. member says.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext:
Will there be enough
vaccine for Alberta, Saskatchewan and Manitoba to meet all the requirements? My understanding is that most of the vaccine will come from the United States.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext:
Importations are being
made by the provinces from the United States, which importations together with the supply produced by the university of Saskatoon, are considered sufficient to deal with the problem.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: Is any subsidy paid by the federal government to the provincial governments so that they can get the vaccine at a lower price and make it available at a reasonable rate? When the epidemic occurred last fall, farmers had to pay atrocious prices for the vaccine to local veterinarians, who themselves had to pay high prices for it. Is the federal government bonusing the provincial governments in this connection?

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext:
No. But the fact that
the provincial governments are supplying the vaccine at cost regulates the price that others can charge.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext:
There is a matter coming under the Animal Contagious Diseases Act which has to do with the regulations under the act governing the cooking of raw garbage to be fed to hogs. This is done in some instances on a very large scale fairly close to the suburban sections of large metropolitan areas, including Toronto. In one of the townships in the constituency I represent, a number of special permits have been issued under the regulations of the Animal Contagious Diseases Act, and it has given rise from time to time to a good deal of criticism and complaints from nearby residents who are affected by these piggeries fairly close to residential properties and farms. I would suggest to the minister, without making any undue criticism of the operation of the regulations, that the . trouble with respect to the location of these plants might largely be avoided if no permits were issued by the dominion unless the consent and approval of the local board of health is first obtained. I realize that in some instances these permits have been granted without the consent and approval of the local board of health, and I make the suggestion in a constructive way to
Supply-Agriculture

the minister in order to avoid difficulties that may arise in future in the operation of the regulations.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: I understand that the health officer of the city has absolute authority in the matter, and that he can exercise his authority with regard to the establishment of any of these feeding places independently altogether of the department. Our permits only make it possible for us to supervise these places; they do not permit the particular thing to be done. The health officer can stop them at any time.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: I think the minister, in referring to the health officers in cities, did not perhaps catch my point exactly, because, so far as I know, there are no piggeries in any city areas; they are usually in townships or rural areas.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: Well, they have health officers too.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: Quite true, they have health officers there, but I think the dominion government might well take it into consideration, that before they issue permits they should have the consent and approval of the local board of health.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: What proportion of this vote is to be devoted to the prevention of bovine tuberculosis? Also, what restricted areas are being tested this year; how many of them are partly completed, and how many are new?

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: The amount of compensation which is here provided for is $390,000, but in addition there is $400,000 in the supplementary estimates, which brings the amount close to $790,000. It is much higher than any previous vote, and is for compensation only.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: To what areas?

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: It covers all Canada, of course; right across Canada, wherever this is being done. Prior to last year Alberta had not taken advantage of it, but now all provinces have done so.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: I want to find out about one or two areas which I know of, which have voted on the matter and voted favourably towards it. Does the minister contemplate doing the work in these areas this year? How many areas have made applications that have been tested; how many does the minister contemplate dealing with this year, and which ones?

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: Perhaps the hon. member would specify the area he has in mind. There is quite a'long list. I may be able to tell him from the list I have before me.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: The particular ones I had reference to are in the Niagara peninsula, including the counties of Haldimand, Lincoln, Wentworth, Brant and Norfolk.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: The order of precedence in which they stand at the moment is: Lanark county, Simcoe county, the townships of Rama and Mara in Ontario county, Waterloo county, Hastings county, Grey county, Norfolk county, Essex county, Haldimand county, Wentworth county, Lennox-Addington county, Brant county and Dufferin county. Those are in Ontario; that is the order in which they stand at present.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: What order is followed in doing the testing in the different counties? Is it according to their precedence in making their application, or is there any patronage in connection with it?

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: What they do usually is to work in blocks, and the area which is already established is widened. That is the natural thing to do, because when an area is established it is much easier to work from that than it is to start in a new county. For example, for many years I was right on the boundary line of an area in western Canada, and I found difficulty in keeping any cattle that I had, separated from the cattle across the road. Naturally, in order to avoid that kind of thing being accentuated, the tendency is to spread out the area you are working in. But apart from that it would be pretty much in the order in which the applications are made.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: The reason I asked that question was this. The county of Lanark stood at the head.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: They are already working there.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: Yes, they are working there now. It is probably two years since a canvass was made of that county to get the farmers to sign up. That was done and they made the application. There appeared in a local paper this spring a notice that, through the influence of the defeated candidate in Lanark county, Lanark county was going to be cleaned up, tested for tuberculosis.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: Hear, hear.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext:
It appeared in all th*
papers that, through the influence of my opponent, who no doubt had the patronage i* Lanark county, that county was being tested. I want to know whether or not the man who has the patronage of the riding has something to do with the testing business or having the tests made.

Live Stock and Poultry

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: I can assure the hon. member for Lanark that his opponent did not ask me to take any action in connection with the matter, and I am assured by the officials that they started in Lanark absolutely on their own initiative.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: Certainly.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: I assume that, if there were any patronage, it would probably have come by the course the hon. member has mentioned, that an attempt would have been made in that direction.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: I should like to ask-and it is not for the purpose of holding up the item- what advance is being made in treating and working upon Bangs disease? In my judgment that is a much worse difficulty to-day in the dairy and live stock industry than tuberculosis. Has any advance been made during the past year?

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: The number of herds under the policy has increased during the last year. Anyone can have his herd tested; that is, we provide the service within reasonable limits, but there is no compensation.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: Is there a suitable serum?

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: No, there is no serum which can be used for treatment.

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: Is the testing made free of charge?

subtopic: SUPERVISION OVER STOCKYARD OPERATIONS- GRADING, INSPECTION AND MARKETING
speechtext: Yes.
